The Aging Parent Legal Documents Checklist

What to locate, talk over with Dad and ask an attorney about.

Download PDF

Dad is managing fine on his own, and nothing is pressing. He signed a will years ago and there may be a power of attorney somewhere, but nobody in the family has seen the papers. Check what you've done. Anything unchecked is something to look for or ask about when it suits him, not a verdict about Dad or his papers.

Locate

Talk over with Dad

Ask an attorney about

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you locate, talk and write down. It doesn't say whether any of Dad's documents is valid, complete or current, or what he should sign or change. Those are questions for an elder law attorney who knows your state. Nothing here is legal, financial or tax advice.

Ready for the next step?

You know which papers to look for, what to talk over with Dad and what to ask about. The planning interview asks about your family's wider situation, of which the legal papers are one part, and gives you a free planning report you can bring to any conversation about paying for care.
